derived.prompt: In a home network, a laptop is directly connected to a router by an Ethernet cable. Does it follow that the router is directly connected to the laptop?
bridge: In a home network, a laptop is directly connected to a router by an Ethernet cable.
chain: In a home network, a laptop is directly connected to a router by an Ethernet cable. (given in prompt)
So the router is not directly connected to the laptop: no, it does not follow.

derived.prompt: A desktop computer is directly connected to a printer by a USB cable. Does that rule out the printer being directly connected to the desktop computer?
bridge: A desktop computer is directly connected to a printer by a USB cable.
chain: A desktop computer is directly connected to a printer by a USB cable. (given in prompt)
So the printer cannot be directly connected to the desktop computer: yes, it is ruled out.

In a home network, a laptop is directly.why: A generic instance: an Ethernet cable joins exactly the two devices at its ends, so the link is the same seen from either end; nothing about these devices is stored.

A desktop computer is directly connected.why: A generic instance: a USB cable joins the two devices at its ends; nothing about these devices is stored.

Wi-Fi is a wireless networking technolog.why: True side fact from the Wi-Fi article.

sources.note: The lead describes Wi-Fi as a family of wireless network protocols based on the IEEE 802.11 standards.

Wi-Fi is a wired networking technology..why: Deliberately false side fact: Wi-Fi is wireless.
